answer: The ferryman stamps one wooden token for every crossing and writes the token's number in the ledger at the landing, and the harbour clerk reads the book against the tokens each evening. A haven token carved at home fails the ledger: at the orchard of the crossing the stamp must match the ferryman's own die, and a home token carries no number. Forging the crossing means bribing the ferryman, carving 400 tokens and paying 8,700, while the shale entry in the ledger is checked nightly, so a traveller whose token was never written is left on the bank.
